reasoning_steps: AirborneWindEnergySystem and VerticalAxisWindTurbine are new concepts that need to be defined based on their descriptions.
The TRL levels for specific technologies like AWES, VAWTs, and floating offshore designs (spar-buoy, semi-submersible) require dedicated classes.

classes.aristotelian_definition: An Airborne Wind Energy System is a type of wind energy technology that uses autonomous kites or unmanned aircrafts to convert wind energy into electricity.
classes.comment: AWES are distinct from conventional wind turbines as they operate at higher altitudes using tethers.

classes.aristotelian_definition: A Vertical Axis Wind Turbine is a type of wind turbine that uses a vertical shaft around which the rotor turns.
classes.comment: VAWTs are less efficient than HAWTs but offer potential in hybrid applications and small-scale installations.

classes.aristotelian_definition: The Technology Readiness Level of an Airborne Wind Energy System indicates the maturity level of this technology.
The Technology Readiness Level of a Spar Buoy Design indicates the maturity level of this floating offshore wind technology.
classes.comment: Spar buoy designs are at TRL 8-9.

classes.aristotelian_definition: The Technology Readiness Level of a Semi-Submersible Design indicates the maturity level of this floating offshore wind technology.
The Technology Readiness Level of a Concrete Barge Design indicates the maturity level of this floating offshore wind technology.
classes.comment: Concrete barge designs are at TRL 7-8.

classes.aristotelian_definition: The Technology Readiness Level of a Tension Leg Platform Design indicates the maturity level of this floating offshore wind technology.
classes.comment: Tension leg platforms are at TRL 6.
